title: Hosted API: Capability Prioritization, Acceptance Matrix, and Rollout Constraints
creator: Sofia Patel
summary: Define prioritized scope, explicit acceptance criteria, and a conservative rollout plan for chat, completions, embeddings and rerank hosted endpoints with clear gating metrics and operational runbooks.
background: Redwood needs a single coordinated PRD that sets a prioritized subset of hosted API features for the next public launch window. Multiple product docs exist focusing on surface design, but there is inconsistent acceptance criteria between teams which risks divergent rollout readiness and customer confusion. This ticket consolidates decisions, defines measurable acceptance gates, and produces a launch checklist that can be followed by PM, Eng, Design, and Support.
goals: Agree on a minimum viable capability set for public hosted API launch across chat, completions, embeddings, and rerank
Produce an acceptance matrix with pass/fail gating metrics for functional, performance, and security requirements
Define a staged rollout plan (canary -> regional scaling -> general availability) with rollback conditions
Deliver an actionable launch checklist and handoff artifacts for support, docs, and partner teams
non_goals: Shipping dedicated or private deployment bundles (separate project)
Complete SDK language parity for all non-core SDKs—we will ship core JS/Python first
Large scale model training or onboarding of new architectures—this is focused on serving and surface stability
product_requirements: Endpoint coverage: chat, completions, embeddings (single and batched), rerank (server-side) must be exposed via REST + OpenAPI spec
API contract stability: response schemas must be versioned and backward compatible unless a major version bump is announced
Authentication: OAuth2 and API keys supported; SSO/SAML enterprise flow documented and validated in private tests
Structured output: function/tool-calling primitives available on chat endpoints with schema validation hooks
Batching & latency knobs: server-side batching must be configurable per-route; default config must meet SLO targets
Quotas & rate limiting: tier-aware defaults + per-customer overrides; error responses must include retry-after headers where applicable
endpoint_specific_requirements: Chat: streaming (chunked) responses, SSE support in REST, conversation state token included for KV cache affinity
Completions: single-turn responses, max_tokens enforcement, temperature/top_p controls, stopping sequences honored
Embeddings: deterministic outputs for same model+input+params; support both single and up-to-8-batch endpoints; embedding dimensionality documented
Rerank: accept candidate lists up to configured max, return score per candidate and stable ranking semantics; provide opt-out for full-text features for privacy-conscious customers
performance_slos: 99th percentile latency for completions (1k tokens) <= 300ms for cached/short sequences under hosted free-tier load profile
Median generation latency for chat (stream resume) <= 150ms per chunk for standard models
Embeddings throughput target: 500 qps per shard with p95 latency <= 70ms for single input
Availability SLO: 99.9% regional during GA for core endpoints (excludes scheduled maintenance)
telemetry_and_observability: Per-route token-level cost and latency metrics in Console
Tracing hooks for request lifecycle (ingress -> model -> response stream) with sampling at 10%
Failure classification: distinguish client error, quota, model OOMs, runtime backpressure, and network errors
Alerting: burn rate alerts for error spikes and latency regressions with documented on-call escalation path
acceptance_criteria: API: OpenAPI spec file committed and published; example requests + SDK snippets for JS/Python included
Compatibility: backward compatibility test suite green across 3 prior minor revisions for response schemas
Performance: load test for target customer profile executed and p95/p99 metrics within SLO budget
Security: threat model review completed and critical/major findings remediated; KMS integration tested end-to-end
Reliability: automated canary pipeline validates new model binary for 72h at canary traffic with zero severity incidents
Docs: Console docs and quickstarts published; migration guide for customers with earlier endpoint variants
Support readiness: runbook (incident + FAQ) authored and triaged with L2 and L3 on-call; training session held
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Internal Staging: Burn-in with internal teams and partner beta customers for 2 weeks
Phase 1 - Canary (5% traffic): Route small percentage of production traffic; monitor canary-specific metrics and automated rollback windows
Phase 2 - Regional Expansion (50% region): Open to more customers in region, enable quotas and limits enforcement
Phase 3 - GA (100%): Full exposure worldwide with pricing and quota tiers; start marketing motion
canary_metrics_and_gates: Error rate delta > 0.5% absolute compared to baseline -> automatic rollback
Latency p95 regression > 30% vs baseline -> hold promotion and trigger perf triage
Client-facing correctness failures (schema mismatch, missing fields) > 0 in canary logs -> fail promotion
Cost burn rate > 150% of predicted budget for canary segment -> pause and investigate caching/batching settings
launch_checklist: Finalize API surface and freeze non-breaking changes
Sign-off from Security on pen-test and KMS integration
Ops runbooks published (on-call, escalation, rollback) and verified via tabletop exercise
Console dashboards for tokens/cost/latency per route are live and pre-populated with synthetic traffic
SDK release candidates (JS/Python) published with migration notes
Billing & quotas pipelines connected and validated end-to-end with test customer accounts
Support FAQ and primary triage playbook published in Knowledge Base
Multi-region deployment validated and health checks automated
migration_and_deprecation_strategy: Provide explicit deprecation timeline for legacy endpoint variants with automated translation layer for 6 months
Offer opt-in compatibility headers for customers who need strict legacy behaviour
Measure adoption and provide targeted outreach for top 50 customers before hard deprecation
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Model OOMs at tail causing request failures -> Mitigation: reserve fallback model variant with lower memory profile and graceful degradation
Risk: Schema changes break downstream SDKs -> Mitigation: strict schema validation in CI + backwards compatibility test harness
Risk: Cost overruns from unbounded batching -> Mitigation: default per-route throttles + billing alerts
Risk: Entitlement or quota misconfig leads to customer impact -> Mitigation: staged rollout with quota enforcement and explicit billing tests
dependencies: Runtime team: batching and KV cache toggles must be available via route config
Console: dashboards and rollout controls implemented and tested
SDK: JS and Python clients with new API surface and streaming primitives
Security: SSO/SAML and KMS integration completion
Legal/Billing: pricing tiers agreed and billing pipeline tested
open_decisions: Final verb names for streaming endpoints (stream vs SSE vs chunked) — decision needed by 2025-02-25
Default batching window (20ms vs 40ms) — leaning 20ms but waiting perf test results
Embeddings batch size max: 8 or 16 — impact analysis in progress
